qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Proprietary solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) stack intellectual property (400+ patents) and long-term on-site service/maintenance contracts create switching costs, but economic returns are structurally depressed by high stack refurbishment/replacement expenses and competitive displacement risks from gas turbines, reciprocating engines, and grid interconnections.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). While Bloom Energy captures strong 'speed-to-power' tailwinds from AI data centres and C&I customers facing multi-year grid interconnect queues, it fails to demonstrate empirical moat proof or economic profitability. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~2.1% (far below the 12% hurdle), burdened by cumulative net losses since inception (accumulated deficit of ~$3.99B through FY2025), high periodic stack replacement costs, and chronic reliance on convertible debt offerings and equity dilution.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year and 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~2.1%, failing the 12% capital efficiency hurdle. Despite top-line revenue scaling from $1.20B (FY22) to $1.33B (FY23), $1.47B (FY24), and $2.02B (FY25), Bloom continues to generate GAAP net losses (-$88.4M in FY25), with GAAP operating margins remaining in low single digits (1.5% in FY24, 3.6% in FY25). Accumulated deficit stood at $3.99B at the end of FY25. Capital structure features heavy use of convertible senior notes (e.g., 2.5% Green Notes due 2025, 3.0% Green Notes due 2029) and repeated debt-for-equity exchanges to manage debt maturities and liquidity.
